document_summary: Newark, NJ Code Title XIX, Chapter 19:2 (Rent Control Regulations; Rent Control Board), part 1 of 3, covering the policy statement, definitions, CPI-based rent increase limits, surcharges, hardship increases, registration and Board provisions. | Part 2 of 3 of Newark, NJ Revised General Ordinances Title 19, Chapter 2 (Rent Control), covering registration, Rent Control Board powers, rent decreases, hearings, surcharges, exemptions for new construction and rehabilitation, the 25% cap on increases, fees and inspections. | Part 3 of Newark, NJ Code Chapter 19:2 (added 5-20-2026) covering rental unit inspections, certificate of habitability, occupancy limits and revocation; it addresses none of the six tracked categories.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: CPI-based annual rent increase cap (§ 19:2-3.1, 19:2-3.2)
rules.requirement: At lease expiration or termination of a periodic tenancy, a landlord may not raise rent by more than the CPI-U percentage increase (CPI 15 months prior to CPI 3 months prior to the month of increase), and never more than 4%. No more than one increase in any consecutive 12 months, with written notice to the tenant and Rent Regulation Officer at least 30 days in advance. No increase is allowed if the dwelling lacks substantial compliance or the landlord has not registered.
rules.coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings as defined in § 19:2-2 are subject to rent control (§ 19:2-2.1). Rent includes parking, pets, furniture, security deposits and similar charges.
rules.exemptions: Public housing; hotel/motel space rented day-to-day to transients; commercial space; newly constructed multiple dwellings and vacant dwellings per §§ 19:2-18.1 and 19:2-18.2; certain federal/state rental-rehabilitation units with Section 8 subsidies (rents capped at HUD fair market rent); units under a preemptive government rent-regulation contract.
rules.interaction: Local rent control; no conflicting state cap is shown in this document. Surcharges for taxes, major new improvements and hardship increases are separate and require substantial compliance and registration.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.extraction_notes: Section history reads 'Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), 9-5-2017; amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I, 09-18-2024'. Month of adoption; exact effective date not stated in source (NJ ordinances generally take effect after final passage and publication). It is unclear whether the 4% ceiling was introduced in 2024 or earlier, so the date is the latest stated amendment. A 2026 amendment (Ord. 6PSF-B, 5-20-2026) touched definitions and registration, not this section.The CPI/4% formula is stated as 'allowable annual increase'.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: 25% annual cap on rent increases
rules.requirement: The Rent Control Board may not grant rent increases above 25% in any one year for any tenant. Increases under the ordinance's rent increase, major improvement and landlord hardship sections within the prior 12 months are added together to test the 25% limit.
rules.key_value: Max 25% increase in any one year (cumulative across increases within 12 months)
rules.coverage_conditions: Dwellings subject to Newark's rent control chapter; rents are controlled at the level received as of the chapter's first adoption on September 4, 1985, with no increases except as the chapter provides.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, vacant properties and substantially rehabilitated dwellings may be exempt under § 19:2-18.
rules.quoted_span: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.extraction_notes: Source history shows only 'Ord. 6 PSF-A(S), 9-5-2017; amended 9-18-2024 by Ord. No. 6PSF-I'. These are amendment history entries, not stated effective dates, so effective_date is null. Per-section standard annual increase (CPI-based) is in § 19:2-3, which is in another part of the document. Section 19:2-21 states rents are frozen at the September 4, 1985 level except for increases the chapter allows.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: new construction exemption from increase limits
rules.requirement: Rent-increase limits do not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for the shorter of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years after construction is completed. The landlord must apply to the Rent Control Board for certification before occupancy.
rules.key_value: Exempt for the lesser of the initial mortgage amortization period or 30 years from completion (30 years if no initial mortgage)
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings; requires a Certificate of Occupancy or Temporary Certificate of Occupancy and an application to the Rent Control Board. The exemption stays with the property on change of ownership.
rules.interaction: Landlord must give prospective tenants a written statement, and include a lease provision, noting the exemption (§ 19:2-24).
rules.quoted_span: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less.
rules.extraction_notes: The history note shows only amendment dates (9-5-2017; 9-18-2024), so effective_date is null. Related exemptions in §§ 19:2-18.2 (vacant dwellings: 5-year exemption after 18+ months vacant and rehab cost over 50% of fair market value) and 19:2-18.3 (substantial rehabilitation: unrestricted initial rent) were amended 5-20-2026 by Ord. No. 6PSF-B.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: rehabilitated vacant unit increase (10% max)
rules.requirement: A landlord who rehabilitates a vacant apartment by spending at least 12 months of the unit's actual monthly rent is entitled to a maximum 10% increase in the actual monthly rent. Only one such increase is allowed per unit in any 12-month period.
rules.key_value: Max 10% increase in actual monthly rent after rehab spending of at least 12 months' rent
rules.coverage_conditions: Vacant apartment units in rent-controlled dwellings; requires an affidavit of expenses, an inspection and abatement of code violations before approval.
rules.quoted_span: Any landlord that rehabilitates a vacant apartment unit by spending a total amount equal to at least 12 months of actual monthly rent per unit will be entitled to a maximum of 10% increase in the actual monthly rent.
rules.extraction_notes: The history note shows only amendment dates (9-5-2017; 9-18-2024), so effective_date is null.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control: retaliatory eviction prohibited
rules.requirement: A landlord may not bring an action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce rights under the rent control chapter.
rules.key_value: Ban on eviction actions in retaliation for exercising rent control rights
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants of dwelling units subject to Newark's rent control chapter.
rules.interaction: Operates alongside New Jersey's Anti-Eviction Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 et seq.), referenced elsewhere in this chapter; the general just-cause grounds are not set out in this part of the document.
rules.quoted_span: No landlord shall bring any action to recover possession of a dwelling unit as a reprisal for the tenant's efforts to secure or enforce any right under this chapter.
rules.extraction_notes: This is a limited anti-retaliation protection, not a full list of just-cause grounds. The history note shows only amendment dates, so effective_date is null.
